manifests", deleted `apps/api.yaml`. The root dutifully pruned the child `stock-api` and, thanks to the finalizer,
deleted its Deployment and Service too: nothing answers in namespace `inventory-stock`, and the warehouse scanners are
failing. `stock-sync` was not part of the commit and is untouched. A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Application `stock-api` is back, managed by `inventory-root`, and the root is Synced and Healthy at the current
head of `main`: Service `stock-api` in `inventory-stock` answers `stock-api v6.2`, Service `stock-sync` in
`inventory-sync` answers `stock-sync v3.4`, and the Deployment `stock-sync` was never restarted. The history of `main`
keeps the accident (nothing is rewritten). Finally every child Application in `apps/` (in Git and live) is protected
against both a mistaken removal of its manifest and the deletion of the root, so that the next accident does not take
a service down.

mission.name: Waves That Do Not Wait
mission.description:
The Beacon telemetry platform is deployed with an app-of-apps: root Application `beacon-root` (repo
`platform/beacon-fleet`, folder `apps/`) creates the child Applications `beacon-db` (sync-wave 1) and `beacon-api`
(sync-wave 2). The database needs about half a minute before it serves, and the runbook says the API must not even
exist until it does. Yet on a fresh bring-up `argocd app get beacon-root` shows both children created within a
second of each other, and `beacon-api` was Healthy while `beacon-db` was still `Progressing`. The waves are in Git,
exactly as the runbook says, and the root sync reported `successfully synced (all tasks run)`.
mission.objective:
The ordering is enforced by Argo CD itself, not by luck: Argo CD must assess the health of the child Applications
(an Application whose status is Progressing or Degraded must be reported as such, an Application resource must
not count as Healthy by default). After a fresh bring-up of the platform from `beacon-root`, Application
`beacon-api` was created only after `beacon-db`'s workload was available. `beacon-root`, `beacon-db` and
`beacon-api` are Synced and Healthy, the children are owned by the root, the waves are still in Git, and
Services `beacon-db` (namespace `beacon-data`) and `beacon-api` (namespace `beacon-edge`) answer
`beacon-db v3.1` and `beacon-api v3.1`.

mission.name: The Permission That Vanishes
mission.description:
Argo CD's own configuration is managed by Argo CD: Application `argocd-settings` (repo `platform/argocd-settings`,
folder `config/`, self-heal on) applies the ConfigMaps `argocd-cm` and `argocd-rbac-cm` in namespace `argocd`.
The payments on-call engineers (SSO group `payments-oncall`) need to be able to sync applications of project
`default` during incidents. An SRE added the permission with `kubectl edit configmap argocd-rbac-cm` and told them
it was done, but a few seconds later the line was gone again and they got `permission denied` once more. Nobody
touched Git. A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Members of `payments-oncall` may `sync` applications in project `default` (and nothing destructive: they may not
delete them), while the auditors' read-only access stays as it is. The change lives in Git and has been applied by
Application `argocd-settings` itself (Synced at the current head of `main`, deployed by a Succeeded sync of that
head, self-heal still on), and the cluster's own settings keep working: the URL, `admin.enabled` and the 60 s
reconciliation timeout are untouched.

mission.name: Staging Before Prod
mission.description:
MeterHub has one root Application per environment, both reading the repo `platform/meterhub-gitops`:
`meterhub-env-staging` (folder `envs/staging/`) and `meterhub-env-prod` (folder `envs/prod/`). Each creates one
child, `meterhub-staging` and `meterhub-prod`, which deploy the service repo `platform/meterhub-service`. The
policy is: staging follows `main`, production runs released tags only, and the last release is `v1.2.0`. This
morning a customer reports the new, unfinished metering code in production: Service `meterhub` in namespace
`meterhub-prod` answers `meterhub v1.3.0-rc1`. A clone of the gitops repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Production runs the release again, deployed through Git and the existing roots: Service `meterhub` in
`meterhub-prod` answers `meterhub v1.2.0`, and `meterhub-prod` is Synced and Healthy at the commit that tag
`v1.2.0` points to. Staging keeps following `main` of the service repo and still answers `meterhub v1.3.0-rc1`.
Both roots and both children are Synced and Healthy, the children are owned by their roots.

mission.name: The Hotfix That Flips Back
mission.description:
Incident on the Courier platform: `courier-routing` v2.4.0 sends parcels to the wrong depot. The fix, v2.4.1, is on
branch `hotfix-routing` of the repo `platform/courier-services` and is not merged yet. The on-call engineer ran
`argocd app set courier-routing --revision hotfix-routing` and watched the fixed version go live. Minutes later the
service answered `courier-routing v2.4.0` again, and every time it is pointed at the hotfix it flips back. The child
Applications come from root Application `courier-fleet` (repo `platform/courier-fleet`, folder `apps/`). A clone of
`courier-fleet` is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
`courier-routing` runs the hotfix and stays on it: it is deployed from branch `hotfix-routing` of `courier-services`
(Synced and Healthy at its head) and Service `courier-routing` in namespace `courier-routing` answers `courier-routing v2.4.1`.
`courier-tracking` is untouched: it still follows `main` and answers `courier-tracking v1.9.0`. The change is made the way the
platform is operated: `courier-fleet` is Synced at the current head of `main` of `courier-fleet`, still with
self-heal on, and owns both children.

mission.name: Rebuild The Platform
mission.description:
The Lighthouse platform cluster was lost and rebuilt: Argo CD is up, nothing else is. Everything that ran there
is described in the Gitea repo `platform/lighthouse-gitops`: AppProjects in `platform/projects/`, one child
Application per component in `platform/apps/` (with sync-waves), and the workloads in `workloads/`. The README
says the platform is brought up by one root Application named `lighthouse-bootstrap`, but its manifest was never
committed, and neither the projects nor the children exist yet (`argocd app list` is empty). The folder
`platform/apps/_archive/` holds a retired component that must stay retired. A clone of the repo is in your
workspace.
mission.objective:
Application `lighthouse-bootstrap` (namespace `argocd`) reads `platform/lighthouse-gitops` and is Synced and Healthy
at the current head of `main`, deployed by a Succeeded sync of that head. Through it, and only through it, the
AppProjects `infra` and `services` and the Applications `lighthouse-cache`, `lighthouse-gateway` and
`lighthouse-catalog` exist; all are Synced and Healthy. The root manages Applications and AppProjects only (not
the workloads themselves), the retired `lighthouse-billing-legacy` is not deployed, and the Services answer
`lighthouse-cache v7.2` (namespace `lighthouse-infra`), `lighthouse-gateway v1.4` (`lighthouse-edge`) and
`lighthouse-catalog v5.0` (`lighthouse-core`).

mission.name: The Missing Region
mission.description:
The edge team runs one `geo-edge` proxy per region, generated from the ApplicationSet `geo-edge` (namespace
`argocd`) and the Helm chart in the Gitea repo `platform/geo-edge`. `argocd app list` shows `geo-edge-us-east`
and `geo-edge-ap-south`, both healthy. Customers in Europe are complaining: nothing answers for `eu-west`,
there is no Application and no namespace `geo-eu-west`, and the ApplicationSet itself reports no error.
A copy of the ApplicationSet manifest is in your workspace (`geo-edge-appset.yaml`).
mission.objective:
The ApplicationSet `geo-edge` generates three Applications `geo-edge-us-east`, `geo-edge-eu-west` and
`geo-edge-ap-south`, each owned by the ApplicationSet, deploying the chart to namespace `geo-<region>` of the
in-cluster destination. All three are Synced and Healthy, and Service `geo-edge` in each namespace answers
`geo-edge <region>` (for example `geo-edge eu-west`).

mission.name: Template Mismatch
mission.description:
The shipping platform keeps one folder per service under `services/` in the Gitea repo `platform/harbor-services`
(`dock-api`, `dock-tracker`, `dock-notify`). A colleague wrote the ApplicationSet `harbor` to turn every folder
into an Application, switching on `goTemplate: true` "because it is the modern syntax". Since then
`argocd app list` is empty, namespace `harbor` does not exist, and the ApplicationSet is Degraded with
"failed to parse template {{path.basename}}: template: base:1: function \"path\" not defined".
A copy of the manifest is in your workspace (`harbor-appset.yaml`).
mission.objective:
The ApplicationSet `harbor` generates one Application per folder of `services/`, named after the folder
(`dock-api`, `dock-tracker`, `dock-notify`), each owned by the ApplicationSet, deploying that folder to namespace
`harbor`. All three are Synced and Healthy, and Service `<name>` in `harbor` answers `<name> v1`
(for example `dock-api v1`).

mission.name: Too Many Apps
mission.description:
The media studio keeps one folder per service under `apps/` in the Gitea repo `platform/studio-platform`, and
the ApplicationSet `studio` turns every folder into an Application in namespace `studio`. The three services
(`render`, `thumbnails`, `captions`) are fine, but `argocd app list` shows a fourth Application, `studio-shared`,
Synced and Healthy but pointless: it deploys a ConfigMap `studio-defaults` into namespace `studio`. Nobody
asked for it: `apps/shared/` only holds build defaults that the CI pipeline reads, not a service.
A copy of the ApplicationSet manifest and a clone of the repo are in your workspace.
mission.objective:
The ApplicationSet `studio` generates exactly three Applications, `studio-render`, `studio-thumbnails` and
`studio-captions`, each owned by the ApplicationSet and deploying its folder to namespace `studio`. There is no
Application for `apps/shared` and ConfigMap `studio-defaults` is gone from `studio`. All three are Synced and Healthy, and Service `<service>` in `studio` answers
`studio <service> v1`.

mission.name: Config Field Typo
mission.description:
Every customer of the portal product is described by a file `tenants/<name>/config.json` in the Gitea repo
`platform/tenant-stack`, and the ApplicationSet `tenant-portals` turns each file into an Application. Last week
`globex` was onboarded and since then nothing is generated for anyone: `argocd app list` is empty and the
ApplicationSet is Degraded with "failed to execute go template {{.namespace}}: template: base:1:2: executing
\"base\" at <.namespace>: map has no entry for key \"namespace\"". A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
The ApplicationSet `tenant-portals` generates one Application per tenant, `tenant-acme`, `tenant-globex` and
`tenant-initech`, each owned by the ApplicationSet, deploying the `chart` folder to namespace `tenant-<name>`.
All three are Synced and Healthy at the current head of `tenant-stack`, and Service `tenant-portal` in each
namespace answers the `message` from that tenant's config (for example `portal globex silver`).

mission.name: Label Me In
mission.description:
The platform team registered a second destination, `staging`, in Argo CD (it is an alias of this cluster's own
API server: `argocd cluster list` shows it next to `in-cluster`). The ApplicationSet `quota-fleet` should deploy
the `quota-api` service from the Gitea repo `platform/quota-service` to every cluster that is labelled
`env: staging`. The ApplicationSet reports "All applications have been generated successfully", yet
`argocd app list` is empty and namespace `quota` does not exist.
mission.objective:
The ApplicationSet `quota-fleet` generates exactly one Application, `quota-staging`, owned by the ApplicationSet,
deploying folder `deploy` to namespace `quota` of the `staging` cluster, and nothing for `in-cluster`. It is
Synced and Healthy, and Service `quota-api` in `quota` answers `quota-api v3`. The `staging` cluster stays
registered under that name.

mission.name: Every Service In Every Env
mission.description:
The mesh team wants every service in `services/` of the Gitea repo `platform/mesh-services` (`invoicer`, `mailer`)
deployed once per environment (`staging` and `prod`). The ApplicationSet `mesh` combines a git directory
generator with a list of environments in a matrix, but nothing is deployed: `argocd app list` is empty and the
ApplicationSet is Degraded with "ApplicationSet mesh contains applications with duplicate name: mailer (and 1 more)".
A copy of the manifest is in your workspace (`mesh-appset.yaml`).
mission.objective:
The ApplicationSet `mesh` generates four Applications, `invoicer-staging`, `invoicer-prod`, `mailer-staging` and
`mailer-prod`, each owned by the ApplicationSet, deploying its service folder to namespace `<service>-<env>`
with Helm parameter `env=<env>`. All four are Synced and Healthy, and Service `<service>` in each namespace
answers `<service> <env>` (for example `invoicer prod`).

mission.name: Overrides Ignored
mission.description:
The ApplicationSet `parcel-api` (namespace `argocd`) generates one Application per environment from the Helm
chart in the Gitea repo `platform/parcel-api`: `parcel-api-dev`, `parcel-api-stage` and `parcel-api-prod`.
A merge generator combines a base list of environments with a short list of per-environment overrides, and
`prod` is meant to be the odd one out: three replicas and the banner `parcel-api prod priority-lane`.
Every Application is Synced and Healthy and the ApplicationSet reports no error, yet production runs a single
pod and still answers `parcel-api prod`. A copy of the manifest is in your workspace (`parcel-api-appset.yaml`).
mission.objective:
The ApplicationSet `parcel-api` still generates `parcel-api-dev`, `parcel-api-stage` and `parcel-api-prod`
(owned by it) with a merge generator, all Synced and Healthy at the head of `main`. Deployment `parcel-api`
in `parcel-prod` runs 3 ready replicas and its Service answers `parcel-api prod priority-lane`; `dev` and
`stage` keep one replica and answer `parcel-api dev` and `parcel-api stage`.

mission.name: Delete The Set, Lose The Fleet
mission.description:
The ApplicationSet `kiosk-apps` (namespace `argocd`) runs the in-store kiosk web app in three regions:
Applications `kiosk-north`, `kiosk-south` and `kiosk-east`, deploying `platform/kiosk-web` to namespaces
`kiosk-<region>`. The platform team's new naming convention is `<team>-fleet`, so the ApplicationSet has to be
replaced by `kiosk-fleet` (same generator, same template, new name — the manifest is in your workspace as
`kiosk-fleet-appset.yaml`). The stores are open: the kiosks must not blink. Nobody dares to type
`kubectl delete applicationset kiosk-apps` — the last time someone did that on another fleet, the kiosks went dark.
mission.objective:
ApplicationSet `kiosk-fleet` exists and generates `kiosk-north`, `kiosk-south` and `kiosk-east` (owned by it, Synced
and Healthy at the head of `main`); the ApplicationSet `kiosk-apps` is gone. The workloads never went away:
the Deployments and Services in `kiosk-north`, `kiosk-south` and `kiosk-east` are the very same objects (same
UIDs) that were running when the mission started, and each Service still answers `kiosk-web v2.4`.

mission.name: The Set Reverts My Change
mission.description:
Production `feedhub-prod` serves `feedhub v1.8` from the `main` branch of `platform/feedhub`. A bug was found and
the fix is sitting on branch `hotfix-1.8.1` waiting for review; the on-call engineer is allowed to run production
from that branch in the meantime (it answers `feedhub v1.8.1-hotfix`). The Application is generated by the
ApplicationSet `feedhub` (namespace `argocd`), together with `feedhub-dev` and `feedhub-stage`. Every time the
engineer points `feedhub-prod` at the hotfix branch (`argocd app set`, the UI, `kubectl edit`), the setting is back
to `main` within seconds. A copy of the ApplicationSet is in your workspace (`feedhub-appset.yaml`).
mission.objective:
Application `feedhub-prod` stays owned by ApplicationSet `feedhub`, tracks branch `hotfix-1.8.1` and is Synced and
Healthy at the head of that branch; Service `feedhub` in `feedhub-prod` answers `feedhub v1.8.1-hotfix`. It must
not flip back by itself. `feedhub-dev` and `feedhub-stage` keep tracking `main` and answer `feedhub v1.8`.

mission.name: Only Prod Gets Auto-Sync
mission.description:
The ApplicationSet `lumen-gateway` (namespace `argocd`) generates `lumen-dev`, `lumen-stage` and `lumen-prod`
from the `platform/lumen-gateway` repo. Release v2 was merged to `main` this morning and nothing happened:
all three Applications are `OutOfSync`, production still answers `lumen-gateway v1`, and somebody has to click
Sync on prod after every merge. The rules of the house: `dev` and `stage` are regression rigs that QA freezes, so
they must stay manual; `prod` must follow `main` by itself (with pruning). The template has no sync policy at all.
A copy of the ApplicationSet is in your workspace (`lumen-appset.yaml`).
mission.objective:
Application `lumen-prod` has an automated sync policy (with prune), is owned by ApplicationSet `lumen-gateway`,
Synced and Healthy at the head of `main`, and Service `lumen-gateway` in `lumen-prod` answers `lumen-gateway v2`
without anyone pressing Sync. `lumen-dev` and `lumen-stage` have no automated sync policy and still answer
`lumen-gateway v1`.

mission.name: Every Repo An App
mission.description:
The mesh platform team wants every repository named `mesh-*` in the Gitea organization `platform` to be deployed
automatically: no Application to write when a new service repo appears. They set up the ApplicationSet
`mesh-fleet` (namespace `argocd`) with an SCM provider generator that lists the organization through the Gitea API,
authenticated with an access token kept in the Secret `gitea-scm-token`. Three service repos exist
(`mesh-pinger`, `mesh-quill`, `mesh-ember`) plus `wiki-notes`, which is not a service. Nothing has been generated:
`argocd app list` is empty and the ApplicationSet is in an error state. A copy of the manifest is in your
workspace (`mesh-appset.yaml`).
mission.objective:
ApplicationSet `mesh-fleet` (SCM provider generator on the `platform` organization of Gitea, repositories
matching `^mesh-`) generates exactly the Applications `mesh-pinger`, `mesh-quill` and `mesh-ember`, owned by it,
deploying `deploy/` of each repo to a namespace of the same name. All three are Synced and Healthy at the head of
`main`, each Service answers `<repo> v1` (for example `mesh-pinger v1`), and there is no Application for `wiki-notes`.

mission.name: Preview Environments
mission.description:
The web team wants a preview environment for every open pull request of `platform/pulse-web` that carries the
Gitea label `deploy-preview`: an Application `pulse-pr-<number>` in namespace `pulse-pr-<number>`, built from the
head of the PR branch and removed again when the PR is closed. The ApplicationSet `pulse-previews`
(namespace `argocd`) uses the pull request generator for Gitea and a token from the Secret `gitea-pr-token`.
There are three PRs: one open and labelled, one labelled but already closed, one open without the label.
Nothing happens: the ApplicationSet reports no error and no preview Application exists. A copy of the manifest is
in your workspace (`pulse-previews-appset.yaml`).
mission.objective:
ApplicationSet `pulse-previews` generates exactly one Application: `pulse-pr-<n>` for the open pull request
labelled `deploy-preview` (branch `checkout-redesign`), owned by the set, deploying `deploy/` at the head commit of
that branch to namespace `pulse-pr-<n>`. It is Synced and Healthy and its Service `pulse-web` answers
`pulse-web checkout-redesign`. The closed PR and the unlabelled open PR have no Application and no namespace.

mission.name: Authentication Required
mission.description:
The `vault-ui` Application in Argo CD has never synced. Its repository, `platform/vault-ui` in Gitea, was made
private last week when the security review flagged it, and since then `argocd app get vault-ui` shows
`ComparisonError: Failed to load target state: ... failed to list refs: authentication required: Unauthorized`.
Platform has already created a read-only Gitea machine user for Argo CD; its details are in
`workspace/handoff.md`. The Gitea admin account is for humans and must not end up inside Argo CD.
mission.objective:
Application `vault-ui` (namespace `argocd`) is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, and
Service `vault-ui` in namespace `vault-ui` answers `vault-ui v2.4`. The repository stays private, and Argo CD
authenticates to it as the read-only machine user, never as `player`.

mission.name: The Secret Argo CD Ignores
mission.description:
Last Friday the platform team created a Secret named `repo-parcel-tracker` in the `argocd` namespace holding
the read-only Gitea credentials for the private repo `platform/parcel-tracker`. It is right there in
`kubectl -n argocd get secret`, with the correct URL, user and password, and yet the `parcel-tracker`
Application reports `ComparisonError: ... failed to list refs: authentication required: Unauthorized`,
and `argocd repo list` does not show the repository.
mission.objective:
Application `parcel-tracker` (namespace `argocd`) is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, and
Service `parcel-tracker` in namespace `parcels` answers `parcel-tracker v0.9`. The repository stays private
and Argo CD reads it as the read-only machine user `argo-reader`.

mission.name: One Secret For The Org
mission.description:
The kiosk platform is five services, each in its own private repository under `platform/`: `kiosk-menu`,
`kiosk-queue`, `kiosk-payments`, `kiosk-signage` and `kiosk-reports`. All five Applications fail with
`authentication required: Unauthorized`. The read-only Gitea machine user `argo-reader` can read every one of them
(password `reader-pass-1Wm6`), and more repositories under `platform/` are coming next quarter. Nobody wants to
register each repository by hand and rotate five passwords later.
mission.objective:
All five Applications (`kiosk-menu`, `kiosk-queue`, `kiosk-payments`, `kiosk-signage`, `kiosk-reports`) are
Synced and Healthy at the head of their repository's `main`, and each service in namespace `kiosk` answers its
version. Argo CD holds the machine user's credentials once, for the whole `platform` organisation, not once per
repository. Repositories stay private.

mission.name: Host Key Verification Failed
mission.description:
The `fleet-agent` Application reads its manifests over SSH, as security asked: the repo URL is
`ssh://git@gitea.gitea.svc.cluster.local:22/platform/fleet-agent.git` and the repository Secret `repo-fleet-agent` in
`argocd` carries a read-only deploy key that Gitea already accepts. Yet the Application never synced and
shows `ComparisonError: ... failed to list refs: ssh: handshake failed: knownhosts: key is unknown`.
Someone suggested "just tick insecure-ignore-host-key"; security will reject that in review.
mission.objective:
Application `fleet-agent` (namespace `argocd`) is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, and
Service `fleet-agent` in namespace `fleet` answers `fleet-agent v5.0`. Argo CD still reads the repository over SSH
with its deploy key, and it verifies the Git server's host key: host key checking is not switched off.

mission.name: Expired Credentials
mission.description:
Mailroom v3.1 was deployed from the private repo `platform/mailroom` and ran fine for weeks. Today the team
pushed v3.2 to `main` and nothing happened: the `mailroom` Application is stuck at the old revision and shows
`ComparisonError: ... failed to list refs: authentication required: Failed to authenticate user`.
The repository Secret `repo-mailroom` in `argocd` has not been touched,
but the Gitea access token it holds was revoked during a security clean-up. Details of the machine user are in
`workspace/handoff.md`.
mission.objective:
Application `mailroom` (namespace `argocd`) is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main` (the v3.2 commit),
and Service `mailroom` in namespace `mailroom` answers `mailroom v3.2`. Argo CD still reads the repository as the
read-only machine user `argo-reader` (not `player`), and the repository stays private.

mission.name: Register A Second Destination
mission.description:
The release team wants the `boarding-pass` API on a destination called `staging`, separate from the built-in
`in-cluster` one. A colleague registered it with a cluster Secret `cluster-staging` in namespace `argocd`: the
same API server under its DNS name `https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local`, authenticating as the
namespace-scoped ServiceAccount `argocd-deployer` of namespace `boarding-stg` (its token Secret lives there).
Application `boarding-pass` targets `name: staging`, but it stays Unknown with
`... tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` and nothing
is deployed. `argocd cluster list` shows `staging` as Failed.
mission.objective:
Cluster `staging` is connected in Argo CD (`argocd cluster list`), it verifies the API server certificate, and
authenticates as ServiceAccount `argocd-deployer` of namespace `boarding-stg`. Application `boarding-pass`
still deploys to that `staging` destination (namespace `boarding-stg`), is Synced and Healthy at the current
head of `main`, and Service `boarding-pass` in `boarding-stg` answers `boarding-pass v3.1`.

mission.name: Namespace Not Managed
mission.description:
Platform registered the cluster `regional` (cluster Secret `cluster-regional` in namespace `argocd`) when only
the EU region existed. Two Applications read the repo `platform/parcel-hub`: `parcel-hub-eu` (folder `eu/`,
namespace `parcel-eu`) is Healthy, but its twin `parcel-hub-us` (folder `us/`, namespace `parcel-us`) was
added today and shows `ComparisonError: Failed to load live state: namespace "parcel-us" for Deployment
"parcel-hub" is not managed`. The ServiceAccount behind the cluster may work in both namespaces.
mission.objective:
Both `parcel-hub-eu` and `parcel-hub-us` stay on the `regional` cluster and in their own namespaces
(`parcel-eu`, `parcel-us`), and both are Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`. The cluster keeps
its namespace scope, limited to those two region namespaces, and keeps authenticating as the namespace-scoped
deployer ServiceAccount. Each Service `parcel-hub` answers `parcel-hub eu v2.0` / `parcel-hub us v2.0`.

mission.name: Waiting For The Poll
mission.description:
The catalog team pushes to `platform/catalog-api` and then waits up to a minute for Argo CD to notice: the
Application `catalog-api` only reacts to the periodic Git poll. The SCM team did add a Gitea webhook on the repo
(push events, JSON, to `http://argocd-server.argocd.svc.cluster.local/api/webhook`), yet Gitea's "Recent
Deliveries" for it are red: HTTP 400 `Webhook processing failed`, and the Argo CD server logs `Gogs webhook HMAC
verification failed` / `Webhook processing failed: HMAC verification failed`. `argocd-secret` already contains a
`webhook.gitea.secret` with the hook's secret. Notes from the SCM team are in `WEBHOOK-NOTES.md`.
mission.objective:
Gitea's deliveries for the webhook of `catalog-api` are accepted by Argo CD (a test delivery from Gitea is logged as
a received push event), while a push event signed with any other secret is still refused, so the endpoint stays
authenticated. The webhook stays active and keeps sending JSON push events to Argo CD. Application `catalog-api`
is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`.

mission.name: Unsigned Commit Rejected
mission.description:
Project `treasury` only deploys commits signed with the team's release key (`spec.signatureKeys`), and Argo CD
has the public key in its keyring. Application `treasury-core` (repo `platform/treasury-core`, branch `main`)
was fine until a colleague pushed "treasury-core v2: same-day settlement window". Now `argocd app get
treasury-core` shows `ComparisonError: GIT/GPG: Failed verifying revision ... by 'ArgoMissions Player
<player@argomissions.local>': unsigned (key_id=)`, the app is OutOfSync and a sync is refused. The release
key's private half lives in a keyring that git in your workspace already uses (the wrapper `gpg-release` next to
the clone), so you can sign.
mission.objective:
The head of `main` in `treasury-core` carries a valid signature from the release key, project `treasury` still
accepts that key and only that key, and Application `treasury-core` is Synced and Healthy at the head of `main`
after a sync Argo CD ran itself. The v2 settlement window (`T+0`) reaches the cluster and Service `treasury-core` in
namespace `treasury` answers `treasury-core v2`.

mission.name: The Leaked Password
mission.description:
The security scanner flagged ticket SEC-2291: the Gitea repo `platform/smtp-gateway` contains a Secret manifest,
`deploy/secret.yaml`, with the real SMTP password in clear text, and Argo CD has been deploying it into
namespace `smtp-gw` since the first commit. Application `smtp-gateway` is Synced and Healthy and the mail relay
works, which is exactly why nobody noticed. Everyone who ever cloned the repo has the password. Security wants the
credentials out of Git without losing the audit trail of what happened, and the gateway must keep running.
mission.objective:
No file at the head of `main` in `smtp-gateway` contains the leaked password or any other Secret data, and the
commit history is untouched (the original leaking commit is still there). Secret `smtp-credentials` in
namespace `smtp-gw` exists with `username` and a new password (never committed to Git, not the leaked one) and
is not managed by Argo CD. The pods of Deployment `smtp-gateway` run with the new value. Application
`smtp-gateway` is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, and Service `smtp-gateway` answers
`smtp-gateway v1.4`.

mission.name: Green Dashboard, Red Backups
mission.description:
Application `vaultline` (repo `platform/vaultline-backups`, namespace `vaultline`) deploys three `Backup`
custom resources of the CRD `backups.vaultline.argomissions.io`. The Argo CD dashboard has shown the
application as Synced and Healthy for weeks, yet the on-call engineer just found out that last night's
ledger backup failed: `kubectl -n vaultline get backups` lists `nightly-ledger` with phase `Failed`, and
`weekly-archive` with `Done`, `hourly-journal` with `Running`. In `argocd app get vaultline` the HEALTH column
of all three Backups is empty. Argo CD never raised an alarm. The vaultline operator owns the `.status` of
these objects; nobody is supposed to touch it.
mission.objective:
Argo CD reports the real health of the Backups of Application `vaultline`: `nightly-ledger` (phase Failed) is
Degraded, `weekly-archive` (phase Done) is Healthy and `hourly-journal` (phase Running) is Progressing,
so the application itself is no longer Healthy. The application stays Synced at the current head of `main`,
and the Backups still carry exactly the status the operator wrote.

mission.name: Every App Is OutOfSync
mission.description:
Since this morning the whole `tallyline` pipeline is OutOfSync: Applications `tallyline-ingest`,
`tallyline-rollup` and `tallyline-gateway` (repo `platform/tallyline`, one folder and one namespace
`tallyline-<folder>` each, automated sync, nobody touched them) flip back to OutOfSync seconds after every
sync. `argocd app diff` of each one shows the same single line: the label `complyd.argomissions.io/scan` is
`pending` in Git and something like `scan-1763300000` on the live Deployment, and the value keeps changing.
The security team's scanner `complyd` (namespace `complyd-system`, a stand-in for the compliance and admission
controllers real clusters run) stamps that label on every Deployment of the pipeline, and it will do so for
every service that is added later too. The security team needs the scanner to keep running.
mission.objective:
Applications `tallyline-ingest`, `tallyline-rollup` and `tallyline-gateway` are Synced and Healthy at the
current head of `main` and stay Synced while `complyd` keeps rewriting the label. The scanner still runs.
The Applications themselves carry no `ignoreDifferences` of their own, and the setting must not hide real
drift of the Deployments (their spec, for one). Each service answers `tallyline-<folder> v4.2`.

mission.name: The Invisible Kind
mission.description:
Application `lexicon-site` (repo `platform/lexicon-site`, folder `deploy/`, namespace `lexicon`) is Synced, yet
its health stays Progressing and the site never comes up: the pod sits in ContainerCreating with
`MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "pages" : configmap "lexicon-pages" not found`. The ConfigMap is in Git,
next to the Deployment, but `kubectl -n lexicon get cm` does not have it and `argocd app get lexicon-site`
lists only two resources and a condition `ExcludedResourceWarning: Resource /ConfigMap lexicon-pages is
excluded in the settings`. A few weeks ago the platform team trimmed Argo CD's `resource.exclusions` to
save controller memory; nothing else on the platform needs to change.
mission.objective:
Application `lexicon-site` is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, ConfigMap `lexicon-pages` in
namespace `lexicon` exists and is managed by Argo CD, the application has no `ExcludedResourceWarning`, and
Service `lexicon-site` in `lexicon` answers `lexicon-site v3.1`. The ConfigMap must not simply be applied by
hand. Argo CD must not be told to watch everything: noisy kinds such as EndpointSlices stay out of its sight.

mission.name: Restart Without kubectl
mission.description:
Finance shipped the new rate card: the ConfigMap `tollbooth-rates` in repo `platform/tollbooth` now says
`tollbooth rates 2025-Q4`, Argo CD synced it, and `kubectl -n tollbooth get cm tollbooth-rates -o yaml` shows
the new value. Application `tollbooth` is Synced and Healthy. Yet Service `tollbooth` in namespace
`tollbooth` still answers `tollbooth rates 2025-Q3`: the pods read the value from the environment when
they started. The pods must be restarted, but the on-call engineer has only Argo CD access for this
cluster, no kubectl rights in production, and nothing in Git needs to change.
mission.objective:
Every pod of Deployment `tollbooth` in namespace `tollbooth` was created after the mission started and
Service `tollbooth` answers `tollbooth rates 2025-Q4`. The restart went through Argo CD (the application's
resource action, as the UI offers it), the Git repo is unchanged, and Application `tollbooth` is still Synced
and Healthy at the current head of `main`.

mission.name: A Button For Maintenance
mission.description:
Before every release of the ticket backend the on-call engineer of the ferry company must put the public
`ferry-booking` Deployment (Application `ferry-booking`, namespace `ferry`) into maintenance mode: the gateway
team's tooling shows a banner while the Deployment carries the annotation `ferry.argomissions.io/maintenance: "on"`
and drops it when the annotation is gone. Today that is a `kubectl annotate` from a laptop, which the security
team wants to end: on-call only has Argo CD. `argocd app actions list ferry-booking --kind Deployment
--resource-name ferry-booking` offers `scale`, `pause`, `restart` and `resume`, nothing for maintenance. The
annotation is operational state and must never be committed to Git.
mission.objective:
For Deployment `ferry-booking` Argo CD offers two actions, `maintenance-on` and `maintenance-off`, next to the
built-in `restart` that on-call still needs. An action is disabled when it would change nothing:
`maintenance-on` while maintenance is on, `maintenance-off` while it is off. Maintenance mode has been
switched on through the `maintenance-on` action (the Deployment carries the annotation, written by Argo CD),
the Git repo is unchanged, and Application `ferry-booking` is Synced and Healthy.

mission.name: Bring Your Own Tool
mission.description:
The label printing service is described by a single `key=value` file, `deploy/app.conf`, in the Gitea repo
`platform/label-printer`. The platform team wrote a config management plugin, `kv-render`, that turns that
file into a Deployment and a Service; it runs as a sidecar of `argocd-repo-server` and its configuration is
the ConfigMap `kv-render-plugin` in namespace `argocd`. The Application `label-printer` (automated sync,
destination namespace `labels-print`) reports Synced and Healthy, yet `argocd app manifests label-printer`
prints nothing and no pod runs. A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Application `label-printer` is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, rendered by a config
management plugin (source type Plugin) from `deploy/app.conf`, and its last sync was done by Argo CD.
Deployment `label-printer` in namespace `labels-print` has 2 ready pods and the Service of the same name
answers `label-printer v2.1`. The repo must still describe the service with `app.conf` only, no hand-written
manifests.

mission.name: Tell Me When It Breaks
mission.description:
The Application `payout-worker` (Gitea repo `platform/payout-worker`, folder `deploy/`, namespace `payouts`)
has been failing its syncs since a bad release (`Service "payout-worker" is invalid: spec.ports[0].port:
Invalid value: 0: must be between 1 and 65535, inclusive`), and nobody noticed for two days: Argo CD only tells
people who look at it. The on-call chat bridge is already running in the cluster as Service `chat-hook` in namespace
`ops-hooks` and accepts JSON `POST` requests on `/hooks/deploys`; it records every request it receives.
`argocd-notifications-controller` is running, but `argocd-notifications-cm` is empty. A clone of the repo is
in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Argo CD notifies `chat-hook` when a sync of `payout-worker` fails: the receiver has logged a `POST` to
`/hooks/deploys` whose body names the application and says the sync failed. The configuration lives in
Argo CD's notifications ConfigMap (a webhook service for the receiver, a template, a trigger) and
`payout-worker` is subscribed to it. Fixing the release itself is not part of this mission.

mission.name: The Defaulted Field
mission.description:
Application `ops-statusboard` (Gitea repo `platform/statusboard-config`, folder `deploy/`, namespace `boards`)
deploys the on-call `StatusBoard` custom resource. Every sync succeeds, and a minute later the app is
OutOfSync again, forever. Nobody changed the board in the cluster and `kubectl` shows the three panels exactly
as in Git. `argocd app diff ops-statusboard` still prints one line that exists only on the live side:
`<     refresh: 30s`. A clone of the repo is in your
workspace.
mission.objective:
Application `ops-statusboard` is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main` after a sync by Argo CD and
stays that way: the persistent difference is gone without hiding the rest of the `StatusBoard` from the
comparison. StatusBoard `oncall` in namespace `boards` still has its three panels and is managed by Argo CD.

mission.name: Forensics With The CLI
mission.description:
Since this week's releases, partner shops report that the `rates-service` API quotes prices in the wrong
currency: `fx-rates v1.2 currency=USD source=ecb`, where it should say `currency=EUR`. Nothing is red:
the Application `rates-service` (Gitea repo `platform/rates-service`, folder `deploy/`, namespace `fx-rates`,
automated sync) is Synced and Healthy. Five releases have gone out in the last days and nobody remembers which
change touched the currency. A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Application `rates-service` is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, deployed by Argo CD, and
the Service `rates-service` in namespace `fx-rates` answers `fx-rates v1.2 currency=EUR source=ecb` with
2 ready pods. The v1.2 release and the later cache TTL change (`CACHE_TTL=600`) must still be in Git, and the
Git history must keep every commit that was released.

mission.name: Why So Slow?
mission.description:
Someone set `timeout.reconciliation: 24h` in `argocd-cm` "to save CPU", and the controller and repo-server were
restarted so it is live. The lobby display board (Application `lobby-board`, Gitea repo `platform/lobby-board`,
automated sync, namespace `lobby`) shows Synced and Healthy and still answers `lobby-board v1.0`, yet release
v1.1 was pushed to `main` a while ago and Argo CD has not noticed. Pressing Refresh makes it appear, but
nobody wants to press Refresh after every push. A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Argo CD polls Git again on a sane schedule: `timeout.reconciliation` in `argocd-cm` is between 30 seconds and
10 minutes (or unset), and both the application controller and the repo-server are actually running with that
value. `lobby-board` is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, its last sync deployed that commit,
and the Service `lobby-board` in namespace `lobby` answers `lobby-board v1.1`.

mission.name: Black Friday Freeze
mission.description:
PAGER, 06:10 — storefront release train is stuck, doors open at 09:00.
Project `blackfriday` runs two Applications from Gitea: `bf-cart` (repo `platform/bf-cart`, namespace `bf-cart`)
and the new sale banner `bf-promo` (repo `platform/bf-promo`, namespace `bf-promo`). Timeline: Monday the
freeze went in; Tuesday the approved `bf-cart` v9.0 landed on `main`; since then `argocd app get bf-cart` is
`OutOfSync` and a manual sync answers `cannot sync: blocked by sync window`. `bf-promo` has never deployed
at all: sync status `Unknown` with `InvalidSpecError: application destination server
'https://kubernetes.default.svc' and namespace 'bf-promo' do not match any of the allowed destinations in
project 'blackfriday'`. Also, the platform team's autoscaler `load-scaler` (namespace `bf-scaler`, not yours,
must keep running) has pushed `bf-cart` to 6 replicas under load, while Git says 2.
On-call already tried: waiting, retrying the sync from the UI, and a long look at the freeze. Nobody dared
to touch the project in the middle of the night. Clones of both repos are in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Both Applications are Synced and Healthy at the current head of their repos: Service `bf-cart` in `bf-cart`
answers `bf-cart v9.0 black-friday` and Service `bf-promo` in `bf-promo` answers `bf-promo v4.0 sale-banner`.
Project `blackfriday` keeps a deny sync window (the freeze stays, an approved manual sync must work) and still
lists its destinations (no wildcard namespace). `bf-cart` keeps self-heal on and holds the 6 replicas the
autoscaler wants without its Deployment spec being rewritten back and forth, and `load-scaler` still runs.

mission.name: First Day On The New Cluster
mission.description:
PAGER, Monday 08:00 — Tidewater payments moved to a new cluster over the weekend. The old one is gone; Argo CD
on the new one is installed and completely empty: `argocd app list` shows nothing, `argocd proj list` only
`default`. Everything that ran before is described in the Gitea repo `platform/tidewater-gitops` (its README
has the new-cluster runbook: one root Application from `bootstrap/`, then the root manages `platform/`:
the AppProject `tidewater` and the three components `tidewater-ledger`, `tidewater-batch`,
`tidewater-gateway`). Since the security review the repo is private. Platform left a handoff note in
your workspace (`handoff.md`) with the read-only machine user for Argo CD.
On-call already tried: reading the README, applying the root from `bootstrap/` ("it says Unknown"), and
creating one namespace by hand to see if that helps. A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Application `tidewater-root` (namespace `argocd`) reads `platform/tidewater-gitops`, is Synced and Healthy at
the current head of `main`, and manages AppProject `tidewater` and Applications `tidewater-ledger`,
`tidewater-batch` and `tidewater-gateway`, all Synced and Healthy at head. Service `tidewater-ledger` in namespace
`tidewater-ledger` answers `tidewater-ledger v3.1`, `tidewater-batch` in `tidewater-jobs` answers
`tidewater-batch v1.8`, `tidewater-gateway` in `tidewater-edge` answers `tidewater-gateway v2.0`. The repo stays
private, Argo CD reads it as the read-only machine user (never as `player`), project `tidewater` stays a
boundary (no wildcard namespace), and the namespaces come from Git: this cluster must be rebuildable from the
repository alone.

mission.name: The Chart Migration
mission.description:
PAGER, Thursday 22:40 — change window for the inventory database migration is open and the on-call is stuck.
`stockroom-db` used to be plain manifests; the migration PR switched Application `stockroom-db-v2` (namespace
`stockroom`, repo `platform/stockroom-db`) to the Helm chart in `chart/`, with production values, and set the
sync policy to manual because it owns a volume. Since the switch `argocd app get stockroom-db-v2` shows sync
status `Unknown` and a `ComparisonError` that ends with `values/prod.yaml: no such file or directory`.
Consumers still call `http://stockroom-db.stockroom` and the volume `stockroom-db-data` holds the inventory data
(`/seq` on the service shows it); the last chart migration, on another team, silently started the database on an
empty volume. On-call already tried: syncing from the UI (same error), and re-reading the PR. Nobody dares to
press Sync with prune. A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Application `stockroom-db-v2` keeps deploying the Helm chart (path `chart`) and is Synced and Healthy at the
current head of `main`, deployed by a Succeeded sync of that head. Deployment and Service are named
`stockroom-db` in namespace `stockroom` (managed by the Application, nothing renamed left over), the service
answers `stockroom-db prod 3.0` on `/` and the original inventory data `seq=4821 shipments=1873` on `/seq`.
The original PersistentVolumeClaim `stockroom-db-data` (same UID as when the mission started) is still the
volume the database uses, and no extra empty claim exists.

mission.name: The Generator Ate The Fleet
mission.description:
PAGER, 03:12 — telemetry is dark. The Orbit fleet (ingest, rollup, alerts) is generated by the ApplicationSet
`orbit-fleet`, one Application `orbit-<service>` per folder of `services/` in the Gitea repo `platform/orbit-services`.
The ApplicationSet itself is deployed by the Application `orbit-control` from the repo `platform/orbit-control`
(folder `appsets/`, automated with prune and self-heal). Timeline: 02:55 a "tidy-up" was merged to `orbit-control`;
02:56 `argocd app list` lost all three `orbit-*` Applications; 02:57 their workloads were deleted and namespaces
`orbit-ingest`, `orbit-rollup`, `orbit-alerts` are empty. `kubectl -n argocd describe applicationset orbit-fleet`
shows no error condition. On-call already tried: pausing the automation of `orbit-control` "so it stops fighting us",
tightening the repositories allowed in project `orbit` "until things calm down", and drafting a force-push that
resets `main` to yesterday: the audit policy says Git history is never rewritten. Clones of both repos are in your workspace.
mission.objective:
ApplicationSet `orbit-fleet` generates `orbit-ingest`, `orbit-rollup` and `orbit-alerts` again (each owned by
the ApplicationSet, Synced and Healthy at the head of `orbit-services/main`, in project `orbit`) and each Service
answers `orbit-<service> v1` in namespace `orbit-<service>`. Application `orbit-control` is Synced and Healthy at the
head of `orbit-control/main` (the fix goes through Git, history only grows: the offending commit stays in the log).
The next generator mistake must not delete workloads: deleting a generated Application must not cascade into
its namespace. Project `orbit` stays restricted to its own repositories and namespaces.

mission.name: Audit Findings
mission.description:
The external auditor's report on the custody platform (Gitea repos `platform/custody-api` and
`platform/custody-batch`, Applications of the same names in project `custody`, namespace `custody`) lists four
findings; everything is "green" today, which is exactly what worries them. Evidence: (1) last week `sam`, a
developer, deleted an Application in the UI and nobody could say why he was allowed to; (2) a database password
is committed in `custody-api` and the repo is cloned on 40 laptops; (3) Argo CD logs in to Git with the human
admin account `player`, one secret per repository; (4) the project `custody` can deploy any cluster-wide kind
("`*/*`"). Yesterday an engineer tried to fix (2) by deleting the Secret with kubectl: Argo CD put it back in
seconds. The release pipeline logs in as `deploy-bot`. Notes with the accounts are in `audit-notes.md` in your
workspace, clones of both repos are next to it.
mission.objective:
All four findings are closed and nothing broke: `sam` can only look, `kim` is still an administrator and
`deploy-bot` can get and sync the Applications of project `custody` and nothing else; no database password is in
the head of `custody-api` and the live Secret `custody-db` holds a different (rotated) password; Argo CD reaches
both private repositories through one credential template for the machine user `argo-reader`, never as
`player`; project `custody` allows exactly the cluster-wide kinds its repositories contain. Applications
`custody-api` and `custody-batch` are Synced and Healthy at the head of `main` and their Services answer
`custody-api v3.1` and `custody-batch v1.2`.

mission.name: The Migration That Ate Monday
mission.description:
PAGE 06:40 - release v7 of `shiftboard` (staff rostering; Gitea repo `platform/shiftboard`, Applications
`shiftboard` from `deploy/` and `rota-crds` from `crds/`, namespace `shiftboard`) was started by hand and stopped:
the sync of `shiftboard` is `Failed` and v6 still answers. The first error was
`Job.batch "rota-migrate" is invalid: spec.template: Invalid value: ... field is immutable`.
06:55 - on-call synced again; this time the PreSync migration hook failed with `Job has reached the specified
backoff limit` and the sync was `Failed` again. 07:30 - the rota for Monday is still the old one, the weekend
shifts have no policy, and the release manager wants release v7 live, plus a pipeline that does not need a
babysitter next release. On-call did not touch the repo. A clone of it is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Application `shiftboard` (namespace `argocd`) is Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, deployed by
a Succeeded sync of that head that ran the migration Job `rota-migrate` and the PostSync smoke test
`shiftboard-smoke` to completion. ConfigMap `schema-version` in `shiftboard` records `v7`, ShiftPolicy
`weekend` has `restDays: 2` in the cluster, Service `shiftboard` answers `shiftboard v7`, and `rota-crds` is Synced and
Healthy at head. The repo is arranged so that the next release does not trip over the same four things,
and the smoke test still tests the service.

mission.name: Drift Storm
mission.description:
PAGE 02:10 - the stormwatch platform (Gitea repo `platform/stormwatch`: `apps/` is read by the root Application
`stormwatch-root`, which creates `sw-ingest` and `sw-alerts`; namespace `stormwatch`) has been "flapping" all
night. `argocd app list` shows the root and `sw-ingest` OutOfSync, `sw-ingest` has not been Synced for longer than
a minute since the mesh team's controller went live, and the rain sensors answer `sw-ingest v2.1-debug`: someone
debugged the Deployment in place. `sw-alerts` still serves `sw-alerts v1.0` although release v1.1 has been in
Git since the evening: during the storm somebody rolled it back with `argocd app set`. Nobody remembers who or
when, and the root, which is synced by hand, never undid it. A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
`stormwatch-root`, `sw-ingest` and `sw-alerts` are Synced and Healthy at the current head of `main`, the children
are managed by the root and `sw-alerts` follows `main` again. Hand edits are undone automatically from now on
(self-heal on the root and on both children, in Git and live). The mesh team's controller `mesh-stamper`
(namespace `stormwatch-mesh`) keeps stamping `sw-ingest` and Argo CD does not mind. ConfigMap `thresholds` has one
owner in Git and holds `rain_mm: "40"` and `wind_kmh: "90"`. Services answer `sw-ingest v2.1` and `sw-alerts v1.1`.

mission.name: Mission Control
mission.description:
PAGE 05:30 - the Meridian transit-signage platform (Gitea repo `platform/meridian-platform`) was rebuilt from Git
overnight: Argo CD, then one root Application, `meridian-root`, reading `bootstrap/`. The root says `Synced`.
Nothing else is right. `argocd app list` shows the root and `meridian-core`, but `meridian-core` has no sync status
and says its project `meridian-core` does not exist; the ApplicationSet `meridian-edge`, which should create the
signage Applications for the districts north, south and harbor, reports
`function "district" not defined`; no signage runs in `meridian-north`, `meridian-south` or `meridian-harbor`.
On-call re-synced the root three times and restarted the ApplicationSet controller. Nobody has touched Git. The
rest of the morning shift starts at 07:00. A clone of the repo is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
The platform is up and reproducible from Git alone. `meridian-root` is Synced and Healthy at the current head of
`main`, maintains the AppProjects `meridian-core` and `meridian-edge`, the Application `meridian-core` and the
ApplicationSet `meridian-edge`, and in Git the projects are applied strictly before what uses them. The
ApplicationSet generates `meridian-edge-north`, `meridian-edge-south` and `meridian-edge-harbor` (each deploying
`edge/` to `meridian-<district>`, Synced and Healthy at head; the Services answer `meridian-edge v3.2`). `meridian-core`
is Synced and Healthy at head, deployed by a Succeeded sync that ran its PostSync smoke test
`meridian-core-smoke`, and creates its own namespace; Service `meridian-core` answers `meridian-core v5.0`. The
projects stay narrow: no wildcard destinations or sources.
